extracted.intended_audience: public water system operators, state regulators, and environmental testing laboratories performing drinking water compliance monitoring
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements for sampling, sample preservation, analytical methods, laboratory certification, monitoring frequencies, compositing, reporting, and compliance determination for contaminants in public drinking water systems under EPA Part 141.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approved analytical methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyses for the contaminants in this section shall be conducted using the methods listed in the table, or the alternative methods listed in appendix A to subpart C of this part, or their equivalent as determined by EPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text incorporates by reference a set of EPA, APHA (Standard Methods), ASTM, and other specific methods and documents (with citation and availability information). Equivalent methods may be used only as determined by EPA; availability and exact method versions are specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard Methods editions and excluded methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific editions of Standard Methods for the Examination of Water and Wastewater (e.g., 18th, 19th, 20th) are authorized for certain methods; certain methods from an edition are explicitly not allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: The following methods from this edition cannot be used: 3111 B, 3111 D, 3113 B, and 3114 B. For some methods the year in the method number designates approval year; only listed online versions may be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method-specific modifications permitted if QC criteria met
rubrics_metrics.description: Substitutions or modifications of method components (e.g., detectors, lamps, flow cells) are allowed provided all regulatory requirements and quality control criteria are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Substitution of detectors in Methods 505/507/508/508.1 allowed to achieve lower detection limits; a 450-W UV lamp may be used instead of 550-W if it provides performance within QC acceptance criteria; modified flow cell configurations allowed if QC acceptance criteria are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample preservation, containers, and maximum holding times
rubrics_metrics.description: Sample collection for listed contaminants shall use the sample preservation, container, and maximum holding time procedures specified in the regulatory table.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The table lists contaminant-specific preservative (e.g., HNO3, conc HNO3 to pH<2, NaOH/pH12, cooling to 4 °C, or none), container type (P = plastic, G = glass), and maximum holding time (e.g., 6 months, 48 hours, 14 days, 28 days, 1 month). Notes clarify cyanide pH 12 adjustment at collection, chilling at 4 °C, acidification options, asbestos container/preservation/holding times per Method 100.2, and that samples should be analyzed as soon after collection as possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sampling location and representativeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Groundwater systems must take a minimum of one sample at every entry point to the distribution system representative of each well after treatment; surface water systems must take a minimum of one sample at points representative of each source or at each entry point after treatment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each sample must be taken at the same sampling point unless another point is more representative. If multiple sources are combined before distribution, sample at an entry point under normal operating conditions (when water representative of all sources is being used).

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring frequency and initial/repeat monitoring schedules
rubrics_metrics.description: Specified initial deadlines and repeat intervals for contaminant monitoring (e.g., analyses by June 24, 1978/1979 for community systems; four consecutive quarterly samples during each compliance period for certain contaminants).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Groundwater systems: minimum one sample per entry point. Surface water: representative points. Community and non-transient non-community systems shall take four consecutive quarterly samples for contaminants listed in §141.61(a)(2)-(21) during each compliance period beginning in the initial compliance period. If initial monitoring completed and no detections, some systems may move to annual sampling; after minimum years States may allow further reduction per specified rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver eligibility and factors for granting
rubrics_metrics.description: A State may grant waivers from specified monitoring requirements after evaluating a set of factors regarding previous use and vulnerability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factors include: knowledge of previous use/transport/storage/disposal of the contaminant in the watershed/zone of influence; previous analytical results; proximity to potential point/non-point sources; environmental persistence and transport; number of persons served and proximity to larger systems; how well the water source is protected (well depth, soil type, wellhead protection; watershed protection for surface water). Waiver conditions: systems granted waivers may have to take one sample per sampling point during the waiver period and update vulnerability assessments; failure of State reconfirmation within 3 years invalidates waiver.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response, follow-up, and reporting for exceedances
rubrics_metrics.description: If an analysis indicates a contaminant listed in §141.11 exceeds the MCL, the supplier shall report to the State within 7 days and initiate three additional analyses at the same sampling point within one month.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the average of four analyses (rounded to same significant figures as MCL) exceeds the MCL, supplier must notify the State (per §141.31) and the public (subpart Q). Monitoring after notification at frequency designated by the State until two successive non-exceeding samples or alternate schedule in variance/exemption/enforcement. Exception: nitrate compliance determined on mean of two analyses; second analysis must be initiated within 24 hours and if mean exceeds MCL report/notify as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance determination procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Compliance with MCLs is determined based on analytical results obtained at each sampling point; specific rules govern averaging, runnings averages, and violation determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If one sampling point is in violation, the system is in violation. For systems monitoring > once/year, compliance is determined by a running annual average at each sampling point. Systems monitoring annually whose sample exceeds MCL must begin quarterly sampling and are not considered in violation until completing one year of quarterly sampling. If any sample causes the running annual average to exceed the MCL, the system is out of compliance immediately. Missing required samples: compliance based on total number of samples collected. Results below detection limit are treated as zero for annual average calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compositing rules and procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: States may allow compositing to reduce number of samples analyzed under specified conditions and with specified laboratory procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Composite samples allowed from a maximum of five sampling points provided the method detection limit is less than one-fifth of the MCL. Compositing must be done in the laboratory and analyzed within 14 days. If composite concentration ≥0.0005 mg/L for any contaminant listed, follow-up samples must be taken within 14 days at each sampling point in the composite. Duplicates from original sampling may be used instead of resampling if holding times permit. Population-based restrictions on compositing (>3,300 persons limited to points within a single system; ≤3,300 may composite among different systems). Detailed lab procedures for compositing prior to GC and GC/MS analyses are specified (volumes, zero headspace, cooling at 4 °C, mixing, purge/desorb, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Laboratory certification requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyses under this section shall only be conducted by laboratories certified by EPA or the State (with provisional certification allowed until January 1, 1996).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To receive certification for specified contaminants, laboratories must analyze Performance Evaluation (PE) samples at least once a year for each method for which certification is desired, achieve quantitative acceptance limits for analytes included in PE samples, and meet MDL requirements. Specific certification sub-requirements are provided for organics and vinyl chloride.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance Evaluation (PE) acceptance limits and organic acceptance criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Laboratories must achieve quantitative results on PE sample analyses within specified acceptance limits for each contaminant; for organics, at least 80% of regulated organic contaminants in PE samples must meet quantitative acceptance limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contaminant-specific acceptance limits are listed (examples: Antimony ±30 at ≥0.006 mg/L; Arsenic ±30 at ≥0.003 mg/L; Barium ±15% at ≥0.15 mg/L; Cadmium ±20% at ≥0.002 mg/L; Mercury ±30% at ≥0.0005 mg/L; Nitrate ±10% at ≥0.4 mg/L; etc.). For organics: achieve quantitative results within ±20% of actual amount when ≥0.010 mg/L and within ±40% when <0.010 mg/L for at least 80% of regulated organic contaminants included in the PE sample.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method Detection Limit (MDL) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Each certified laboratory must determine the method detection limit (MDL) at which it is capable of detecting VOCs (and other analytes) according to appendix B to part 136; the acceptable MDL is 0.0005 mg/L.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This MDL concentration (0.0005 mg/L) is the detection concentration for purposes of this section. Certification requires achieving MDLs per procedures in appendix B to part 136.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special vinyl chloride certification requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: To receive certification to conduct analyses for vinyl chloride the laboratory must meet additional PE and MDL requirements and hold certification for the range of contaminants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements: analyze PE samples at least once a year for each method desired; achieve quantitative PE results within ±40% of the actual amount of vinyl chloride in the PE sample; achieve MDL of 0.0005 mg/L per appendix B to part 136; obtain certification for contaminants listed in §141.61(a)(2)-(21).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compositing follow-up and duplicate sample provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: If composite sample concentration triggers follow-up or if duplicates exist, specific options apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If composite ≥0.0005 mg/L then follow-up samples must be taken within 14 days at each sampling point included. If duplicates of the original samples from each sampling point are available, the system may use these instead of resampling, provided duplicates are analyzed and results reported to the State within 14 days and holding times are not exceeded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Population-based compositing restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Population size of the system affects compositing permissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If population served >3,300 persons, compositing may only be permitted by the State at sampling points within a single system. In systems serving ≤3,300 persons, the State may permit compositing among different systems provided the 5-sample limit is maintained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring escalation and de-escalation based on detections
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems detecting contaminants above detection thresholds must increase monitoring frequency; systems demonstrating sustained compliance may apply for reduced monitoring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a contaminant in §141.61(a)(2)-(21) is detected at ≥0.0005 mg/L, the system must monitor quarterly at each sampling point with a detection. The State may decrease quarterly monitoring if the system is determined reliably and consistently below MCL, but only after minimum samples (groundwater: at least two quarterly samples; surface water: at least four). Systems reliably below MCL may be allowed to monitor annually, during previously highest-result quarters. Systems with three consecutive annual samples with no detection may apply for waiver per paragraph (f)(7). Systems that violate requirements must monitor quarterly; after a minimum of four consecutive quarterly samples showing compliance, the system may reduce monitoring per (f)(11)(iii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of historical monitoring data for initial compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: States may allow use of monitoring data collected after January 1, 1988 required under section 1445 of the Act for initial monitoring compliance if data are generally consistent with other requirements of this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such data (e.g., a single sample rather than four quarterly samples) may be used to satisfy the initial monitoring requirement. Systems using grandfathered samples with no detections shall begin annual monitoring in accordance with paragraph (f)(5) beginning with initial compliance period.

rubrics_metrics.name: State authority to increase monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: States may increase required monitoring where necessary to detect variations within the system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is discretionary authority for the State to require more frequent monitoring than the baseline regulatory schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Atrazine immunoassay (Syngenta AG-625) confirmatory testing requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of Syngenta Method AG-625 for atrazine has restrictions and confirmatory testing requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This method may not be used where chlorine dioxide is used for drinking water treatment. In other systems, any result for atrazine by Method AG-625 greater than one-half the MCL (>0.0015 mg/L) must be confirmed using another approved method and should use additional volume of the original sample collected for compliance monitoring. When AG-625 triggers confirmatory testing, the confirmatory result is used to determine compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sulfide interference advisory for cyanide methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Low sulfide levels may produce positive interferences in cyanide methods using lead acetate paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test samples using a more sensitive sulfide method to determine if sulfide interference is present and treat samples accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct analysis vs. preconcentration effect on MDLs and required preconcentration
rubrics_metrics.description: MDLs reported in some EPA methods were determined using preconcentration steps during sample digestion; MDLs determined when samples are analyzed by direct analysis (no digestion) will be higher.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For direct analysis of cadmium and arsenic by Method 200.7, and arsenic by Method 3120 B, sample preconcentration using pneumatic nebulization may be required to achieve lower detection limits. Preconcentration may also be required for direct analysis of antimony, lead, and thallium by Method 200.9; antimony and lead by Method 3113 B; and lead by Method D3559-90D, unless multiple in-furnace depositions are made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arsenic ultrasonic nebulization requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If ultrasonic nebulization is used for arsenic determination by Method 200.8, the arsenic must be in the pentavalent state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For direct analysis of arsenic with Method 200.8 using ultrasonic nebulization, samples and standards must contain 1 mg/L of sodium hypochlorite to provide uniform signal response.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCBs identification and measurement note
rubrics_metrics.description: PCBs are qualitatively identified as Aroclors and measured for compliance as decachlorobiphenyl; method users may face differing detection limit performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PCBs as Aroclors measured for compliance as decachlorobiphenyl. Users of Method 505 may have more difficulty achieving required detection limits than users of Methods 508.1, 525.2 or 508.
